en: The Therāpadāna, Paṇṇadāyakavagga 3. The Apadāna of the Elder Paccuggamaniya I went forth from home into homelessness, Having heard the teaching of the Buddha. Then, having seen the Teacher, the Great Sage, I approached him with palms joined together. “O Blessed One, I am one who has gone forth; I have come before you, O Knower of the World. Having spoken thus to the Teacher, the Great Sage, I stood before him with palms joined together. The Teacher, knowing my intention, Spoke these words to me, the Elder: “Come, monk,” he said, and that very moment My head was shaven and my robes were on. Having become a monk, I lived in seclusion, Devoted to meditation day and night. Then, having attained the state of an Arhat, I dwelt in the bliss of liberation. I have reached the end of suffering, Cooled, taintless, and free from craving. This is my final birth; There will be no further existence for me. Thus did I speak this verse In the presence of the Tathāgata. By that root of merit, O Blessed One, May I attain Nirvāṇa in the future.

Through the power of that deed, And through the grace of the Buddha, I have attained the fruit of Arhatship, And I have reached the end of suffering. May all beings be well and happy; May they be free from enmity and fear. May all beings look upon each other With minds full of loving-kindness. May all beings be joyful and at peace; May no harm come to anyone anywhere. Just as a mother protects her own child, So should one cultivate boundless love for all beings. May all beings be safe and secure; May all beings be free from distress. May all beings find happiness; May all beings be free from suffering. Thus did I speak this verse In the presence of the Tathāgata. By that root of merit, O Blessed One, May I attain Nirvāṇa in the future. “Like a forest-dwelling lion,
like a noble bull,
like a hump-backed one shining with splendor— ”
The bull among men was approaching—
Siddhattha, the light of the world,
the healer of all the world.
With a mind full of serene confidence, I went out to meet him.
Ninety-four aeons ago,
I went out to meet that bull among men;
I do not know a state of woe—
this is the fruit of going out to meet him.
In the thirty-seventh aeon from now,
I was once a lord of men named Saparivāra.
A wheel-turning monarch of great power.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth].
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
In this way, it is said, the venerable elder Paccuggamaniya recited these verses.
This is the third legend of the elder Paccuggamaniya.
